key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent complex dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules from molecular structure, capturing both dispersive and absorptive optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster screening of photoactive molecules for optoelectronic device design by reducing reliance on costly TD-DFT calculations.
method: Uses 3D molecular geometry and UV-vis spectra as inputs
Employs an equivariant GNN to predict tensor-valued, frequency-dependent polarizabilities
Validates predictions on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic molecules and in device-level optical simulations
evidence_signal: The model reproduces key dynamic polarizability features across datasets and achieves agreement with TD-DFT-based charge carrier generation rates in downstream device simulations with R^2 = 0.94.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on the availability and quality of structural and spectral inputs, so out-of-distribution molecules or incomplete spectra could reduce reliability.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
